sources.title: Ja 547 The Birth Story about (the Great King) Vessantara (Mahānipāta)
sources.edition: Cowell, The Jataka vol. VI, no. 547 (Ja 547 Vessantarajātaka); page markers [6.xxx] follow Cowell vol. VI

facts.subject: ja547
facts.object: The Teacher told this story near Kapilavatthu, about a shower of rain
facts.statement_vi: Theo Ja 547 (Cowell), Đức Phật kể truyện này khi ở gần Kapilavatthu, tại Rừng Đa, nhân một trận mưa.

evidence.span: This story the Teacher told while dwelling near Kapilavatthu in the Banyan Grove, about a shower of rain.

facts.subject: vessantara
facts.object: Vessantara (named because born in Vessa Street, the merchant quarter)
facts.statement_vi: Theo Ja 547 (Cowell), Vessantara sinh ở phố Vessa nên được đặt tên như vậy.

evidence.span: On [6.251] his name-day, because he was born in the Vessa Street, they gave him the name Vessantara
the newborn prince and heir was named Viśvantara (Vessantara), which means 'Born in the merchant quarter'.

facts.subject: vessantara
facts.object: paccaya
facts.statement_vi: Theo Ja 547, đúng ngày Vessantara ra đời, một voi cái bay mang đến con voi con trắng toàn thân, đặt trong chuồng hoàng gia; đặt tên Paccaya.

evidence.span: On his very birthday, a female flying elephant brought a young one, esteemed to be of lucky omen, white all over, and left it in the royal stables.
On the same day, a female elephant brought her newborn calf to the royal palace. The calf was pure white.

facts.subject: vessantara
facts.object: as a child gave away his hundred-thousand-piece necklace to his nurses, nine times
facts.statement_vi: Theo Ja 547, khi còn nhỏ (4-5 tuổi) Vessantara cho người nhũ mẫu chiếc vòng cổ trị giá trăm nghìn đồng, và làm vậy chín lần.

evidence.span: But the prince still in his childhood gave this also to his nurses, and so nine times over.

facts.subject: vessantara
facts.object: maddi
facts.statement_vi: Theo Ja 547, lên 16 tuổi, Vessantara cưới Maddī (chị em họ) làm hoàng hậu và được tôn làm vua.

evidence.span: from the family of king Madda they brought his first cousin, named Maddī, with sixteen thousand attendant women, and made her his queen consort

facts.subject: vessantara
facts.object: gave alms of six hundred thousand pieces of money each day as king
facts.statement_vi: Theo Ja 547, sau khi nhận ngôi, mỗi ngày Vessantara bố thí sáu trăm nghìn đồng tiền.

evidence.span: From the time of his receiving the kingdom he distributed much alms, giving each day six hundred thousand pieces of money.

facts.subject: vessantara
facts.object: jali
facts.statement_vi: Theo Ja 547, hoàng hậu Maddī sinh con trai, đặt trong võng vàng nên đặt tên là Jāli.

evidence.span: brought forth a son, and they laid him in a golden hammock, for which reason they gave him the name of prince Jāli [Net].

facts.subject: vessantara
facts.object: kanhajina
facts.statement_vi: Theo Ja 547, con gái được đặt trong tấm da đen nên đặt tên là Kaṇhājinā.

evidence.span: the queen bore a daughter, and they laid her in a black skin, for which reason they gave her the name of Kaṇhājinā [Black Skin].

facts.subject: kalinga_king
facts.object: Go and fetch Vessantara's elephant (sent eight brahmins because of drought)
facts.statement_vi: Theo Ja 547, xứ Kāliṅga hạn hán, vua sai tám bà-la-môn đi xin con voi trắng của Vessantara.

evidence.span: Go and fetch Vessantara’s elephant.”
Now at that time there was drought in the kingdom of Kāliṅga: the corn grew not, there was a great famine

facts.subject: vessantara
facts.object: gave the white elephant with all its ornaments and five hundred attendants to the brahmins
facts.statement_vi: Theo Ja 547, Vessantara tặng con voi trắng cùng đồ trang sức và năm trăm tuỳ tùng cho các bà-la-môn.

evidence.span: all these he gave to the brahmins; besides five hundred attendants with the grooms and stablemen

facts.subject: sivi_citizens
facts.object: Vessantara
facts.statement_vi: Theo Ja 547, dân thành giận vì việc cho voi nên trục xuất Vessantara; chính ông nói họ trục xuất ông vì món quà con voi.

evidence.span: they banish me for the gift of the elephant.
All angry at your giving gifts, and therefore banish you.”

facts.subject: vessantara
facts.object: asked a day of delay to give the great gift of the seven hundreds (700 elephants, horses, chariots, girls, cows, slaves)
facts.statement_vi: Theo Ja 547, trước khi đi đày Vessantara xin hoãn một ngày để làm lễ đại thí bảy trăm (voi, ngựa, xe, thiếu nữ, bò, nô lệ).

evidence.span: You must get ready seven hundred elephants, with the same number of horses, chariots, girls, cows, men slaves and women slaves

facts.subject: vessantara
facts.object: vanka
facts.statement_vi: Theo Ja 547, Vessantara rời thành đi lên núi Vaṅka cùng Maddī và hai con.

evidence.span: That since he now does banish me, to Vaṅka hill I go.
took leave, and with her two children went before Vessantara and took her place in the carriage.

facts.subject: vessantara
facts.object: Jūjaka
facts.statement_vi: Theo Ja 547, khi Jūjaka xin hai con, Vessantara vui lòng cho, bảo mình không do dự.

evidence.span: I give, and shrink not: you shall be their master.
When the Great Being had made the gift, he was joyful, thinking how good a gift he had made, as he stood looking upon the children.

facts.subject: jujaka
facts.object: bound the boy's right hand to the girl's left with a creeper and drove them away, beating them
facts.statement_vi: Theo Ja 547, Jūjaka lấy dây leo trói tay phải của bé trai vào tay trái của bé gái rồi vừa đánh vừa đuổi đi.

evidence.span: with it he bound the boy’s right hand to the girl’s left, and drove them away beating them with the ends of the creeper.

facts.subject: sakka
facts.object: took the form of a brahmin to beg Maddī from Vessantara, intending to give her back
facts.statement_vi: Theo Ja 547, Sakka hoá thành bà-la-môn xin Maddī, định sau đó trả lại.

evidence.span: Well, then, I will take the form of a brahmin, and beg for Maddī.
I shall make it impossible that she should be given to anyone else and then I will give her back.
Fearing that Vessantara would give away his wife as well, the deity Śakra intervened and in disguise, asked for his wife Madri

facts.subject: sakka
facts.object: gave Maddī back to Vessantara and offered eight boons
facts.statement_vi: Theo Ja 547, Sakka trả lại Maddī và ban tám điều ước; Vessantara xin hoà giải với cha và được triệu về.

evidence.span: “Sir, now I give you Maddī back, your fair and lovely wife,
Choose you a boon, O royal sage, eight boons I give to you.”

facts.subject: sanjaya
facts.object: Jūjaka
facts.statement_vi: Theo Ja 547, vua Sañjaya chuộc hai cháu từ Jūjaka và nhận lỗi đã trục xuất con.

evidence.span: The king bade pay the price for the children.
The king acknowledged his fault:

facts.subject: sakka
facts.object: rained the seven kinds of jewels over the palace and city on the night Vessantara returned
facts.statement_vi: Theo Ja 547, khi Vessantara hồi cung, Sakka làm mưa bảy báu phủ cung điện và thành phố.

evidence.span: He brought down a rain of the seven kinds of jewels like a thundershower

facts.subject: buddha
facts.object: vessantara
facts.statement_vi: Theo Ja 547, Đức Phật nhận diện kiếp trước: vua Vessantara là chính Ngài; Jūjaka là Devadatta; Maddī là mẹ Rāhula; Jāli là Rāhula; Kaṇhājinā là Uppalavaṇṇā.

evidence.span: Rāhula’s mother was queen Maddī, Rāhula was prince Jāli, Uppalavaṇṇā was Kaṇhājinā
Devadatta was Jūjaka
king Vessantara was I myself.
